newsitem.title: UK: IPE gas oil closes firm, Brent touches daily high.
newsitem.headline: IPE gas oil closes firm, Brent touches daily high.

text.p: Driven by supply fears, IPE prompt gas oil closed sharply higher on Friday, while Oct Brent touched a session high in late on nervous trade buying, dealers said.
Sep gas oil settled up $7 a tonne at $219.75, 75 cents off the day's high. The Sep/Oct backwardation closed at $9.25, having narrowed from a gulf of $11.75 earlier in the session.
Oct Brent was trading 25 cents up at $22.41 a barrel by 1645 GMT, having briefly brushed a high of $22.50 moments earlier.
"It's the same pattern that we've been seeing all week, it's all nerves over Iraq." said one broker.
"We're seeing some heavy trade buying... coming into the weekend nobody wants to be short," said another dealer.
But gas oil continued to accelerate away from crude, with the Oct crack spread trading firmer at $5.76 a barrel.
Brokers said that supply tightness in northwest Europe had sparked fears of a shortage of prompt material for delivery against the screen when the Sep contract expires next Thursday.
"Gas oil is a different story, (a trading house) is taking are taking advantage of tight fundamentals to go for the squeeze," said an IPE floor broker.
Forty percent of the European Union gas oil pool will change over to 0.05 percent sulphur on October 1.
Brokers said that this was causing a natural supply tightness for 0.2 percent material, which the IPE will continue to quote.
